Q: How to keep "git pull" from deleting local files A:

I am late with the answer but I had the same issue on Windows when running git pull:

Deletion of directory '...' failed. Should I try again? (y/n)

In my case, the pull was blocked because Git could not delete some directories, usually because another process had a handle on them. If you just want Git to answer "no" to every retry prompt and continue the pull, you can pipe `n` into the command:

yes n | git pull

Q: Updating Due Date based on Invoice Date and Vendor A:

The due date should be calculated automatically using the invoice date and the vendor’s agreed payment terms. For example, if a vendor has Net 30 terms and the invoice date is August 1, the due date would be August 31.

If a vendor has different payment terms, such as Net 15, Net 45, or Net 60, the system should apply the appropriate terms automatically. This reduces manual data entry, prevents incorrect due dates, and helps AP teams avoid late payments while taking advantage of early-payment discounts.

Q: Can I insert a blank line after each file is processed with gnu `find`? A:

A bit late to the party, but based on the answer of RavinderSingh13 and OP's first try, one alternative approach could be:

find . -name eval_results.txt -printf "\n" -print -exec cat {} \;

Explanation of the command:

  • find . looks for any file/folder in the current working directory (.)

  • -name eval_results.txt restricts the results to only those that end in eval_results.txt . Note: this could be a folder too, as no file type was specified.

  • -printf "\n" will add a new line before every command.

  • -print will print the name of each file that is found.

  • -exec cat {} \; will execute the cat command for every file found.

    • {} here represents the path to the found file.

    • \; here indicates the end of the command to be executed with -exec .

    • Note: any options for printing are only interpreted if they occur before the exec command.

Note: this was only tested with find (GNU findutils) 4.8.0

Q: moviepy enlarging and zooming in video outputs A:

from moviepy import VideoFileClip, vfx

src="/mnt/data/1000230922.mp4"

out="/mnt/data/video_resume_adjusted.mp4"

clip = VideoFileClip(src)

# Gentle professional colour adjustment + subtle fades.

adjusted = clip.with_effects([

vfx.MultiplyColor(1.05),

vfx.FadeIn(0.15),

vfx.FadeOut(0.20)

])

adjusted.write_videofile(

out,

codec="libx264",

audio_codec="aac",

preset="medium",

threads=2,

logger=None

)

clip.close()

adjusted.close(

)

print(f"Done: {out}")
